decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and thermal conductivity. Various processing techniques such as mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and laser powder bed fusion have been employed to synthesize HEAs. The effects of alloying elements, milling time, and sintering temperature on the microstructure and properties of HEAs have been investigated. Recent studies have also explored the use of molecular dynamics simulations to understand the evolution of chemical short-range order and its impact on thermal conductivity.
decision.unsolved: Despite significant progress, there is still a lack of understanding of the relationships between the composition, processing, and properties of HEAs. The development of HEAs with optimized properties for specific applications remains a challenge. Further research is needed to explore the potential of HEAs for superconducting properties and to understand the underlying mechanisms.
